extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, equity practitioners, and judges considering interlocutory injunctions in patent infringement cases
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and discretionary factors courts apply when deciding whether to grant, continue, dissolve, or refuse a temporary/interlocutory injunction to restrain alleged patent infringement, across different stages of hearing and evidentiary postures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lord Eldon rule — injunction on patent plus exclusive possession
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent has been granted, and there has been an exclusive possession of some duration under it, the court will interpose its injunction, without putting the party previously to establish the validity of his patent by an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule supports granting an injunction prior to trial when issuance of the patent plus evidence of exclusive enjoyment/possession for some time creates a prima facie right. Exceptions arise where defects are glaring or the patent is very recent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissued/amended patent prima facie evidentiary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patentee has surrendered his original patent and taken out another with an amended specification, the action of the commissioner in granting the subsequent patent is prima facie evidence that the two patents are for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a grant can only be invalidated by clear proof of fraud, excess of authority, or manifest discrepancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent ('patent of yesterday') patents require trial on validity if defects alleged
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent is but of yesterday, and it is endeavored to be shown that there is no good specification or that the patent ought not to have been granted, the court will not, from its own notions, act upon the presumed validity or invalidity without the right having been ascertained by a previous trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts are reluctant to resolve substantial validity issues on an interlocutory application when the patent is recent and alleged defects are significant; the patentee will be sent to law to establish validity before receiving injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Washington's test — clear right verified by affidavit
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice is to grant an injunction upon the filing of the bill, and before a trial at law, if the bill state a clear right, and verify the same by affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the bill states an exclusive possession of the invention (e.g., use or sales), an injunction may be granted even if the court has doubts about validity; conversely glaring defects in the patent/specification will preclude such relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office action not conclusive where subsequent patent issued without notice
rubrics_metrics.description: When the defendant in his answer merely sets up a subsequent patent granted to himself (without impeaching validity of the first), the action of the commissioner in granting the subsequent patent without notice is not conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Office's ex parte opinion may indicate officers' views but is not binding; courts may grant interlocutory injunctions despite contrary expert opinion at the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three evidentiary classes for injunction applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases are to be ranged under three classes: (1) nothing before the court but bill and affidavits; (2) injunction asked before final hearing and respondent offers evidence (answer/affidavits); (3) question on hearing with full proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different standards and weights are applied depending on which evidentiary posture the case presents; the treatise analyzes each class separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements where only bill and affidavits are presented
rubrics_metrics.description: When the plaintiff asks for an injunction upon the bill and affidavits and no opposing evidence is adduced, the bill and affidavits must show the issuing of the patent and an exclusive possession of the right of some duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these are shown, the injunction will be granted without a prior trial at law; but glaring defects in the patent or material defects in the bill will defeat the application. Additional supporting evidence (e.g., uninterrupted use/sale) strengthens the prima facie case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long use/possession and prior enforcement as additional evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that after procuring the patent the plaintiff put the right into exercise or use for some time without being disturbed, and that the patentee has successfully prosecuted others for violating it, strengthens the probability that the patent is good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such enjoyment/possession and recoveries can alone often justify issue of an injunction; courts consider length and character of enjoyment (examples range from a few years to decades) in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original letters-patent and entitlement to temporary injunction on extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee has established his title under original letters-patent, he is entitled to a temporary injunction under an extension of those letters-patent, without a trial at law or evidence of long possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An existing, established title can carry strong equitable protection in interlocutory relief even absent long public use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation-of-instrument cases decided on their writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the right to a temporary injunction depends upon the interpretation to be put upon a written instrument, it is the duty of the court to interpret it and to grant or refuse the injunction accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts normally construe deeds or licenses and act on that construction, but may suspend decision if there are grave doubts about the instrument's legal effect and surrounding circumstances counsel waiting for final hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex mechanical comparisons may preclude summary determination
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not sufficient merely to produce the machine of the plaintiff and that of the defendant and submit them to an examination and comparison by the court, at least where such a comparison would involve more than the usual amount of mechanical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the comparison requires technical expertise beyond the court's capacity in an interlocutory posture, an action/trial may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors when opposing evidence is offered (displacement of prima facie right)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the injunction is asked before the hearing but opposing evidence is adduced, the court weighs: how far and for what length there has been exclusive possession; how far the respondent has raised doubts as to novelty, patentable subject, or infringement; and how far long possession counters impeachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a prima facie right to an injunction where patent, long possession, and infringement are shown; the question becomes whether the respondent's evidence displaces that presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee who accepted partial assignment cannot attack patent validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patentee has made a partial assignment and entered into an agreement with the assignee in the nature of a copartnership, the assignee cannot, in a bill for an injunction, deny the validity of the patent or set up an outstanding patent bought from a third party to impeach originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable estoppel/related doctrines may prevent an assignee from contesting the assigned patent in an injunction suit brought on its strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of presumption when possession and recoveries exist
rubrics_metrics.description: When presumption in favor of validity is strengthened by enjoyment and possession undisturbed for several years, and recoveries against others, mere affidavits casting doubt on originality will not suffice to deprive plaintiff of injunction before trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee must present something stronger than mere issue of the patent; courts often treat lengthy, undisputed use plus successful enforcement as a powerful color of title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of counter-affidavits alone when presumption strong
rubrics_metrics.description: If long possession, use, sales, and prior judgments support the patentee, affidavits read by the respondent tending to cast doubt on originality are often insufficient to annul the patentee's claim to an interlocutory injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because preliminary affidavits are taken without cross-examination, courts require substantial opposing proof to overturn strong presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No injunction before trial where counterbalancing circumstances lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: If the counterbalancing and fortifying circumstances of long possession, use, or sale, and former recoveries under the patent do not exist, the injunction will not be allowed before trial when doubts are raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of strong, historical indicia of validity means the presumption of good title is weaker and a trial is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laches by patentee defeats interlocutory relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patentee has been guilty of laches in not bringing his injunction bill (e.g., knew of infringement long before filing), the court will not entertain a motion for an interlocutory injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay and acquiescence that prejudice the defendant's position or indicate lack of urgency weigh heavily against granting interim equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting evidence on possession and novelty requires trial
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent succeeds in raising doubts both as to exclusive possession and novelty, and the evidence on these points is conflicting, the injunction will be refused until a trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When both the foundational elements of the presumption are challenged with conflicting proofs, equity will defer to a full adjudication at law or on final hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in law (anticipation) can peremptorily defeat injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue of novelty may be raised by alleging a so-called publication in law (e.g., a foreign book sent here for sale) which, if proved, can warrant a peremptory refusal of the patentee's application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual legal publication prior to the patentee's specification is decisive on novelty irrespective of how many persons actually used the disclosure; courts will dismiss injunctions where such anticipation is shown as a matter of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doubt as to infringement requires trial by jury
rubrics_metrics.description: If the question of infringement is doubtful, it must be tried by a jury; courts have dissolved injunctions and ordered actions to try infringement, sometimes with interim accounting orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A feigned issue or jury trial is not a matter of right — the applicant must lay a foundation showing a real need for a jury opinion; ultimately, it is for the court to decide whether to send the question to a jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on defendant's business and irreparable harm balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the injunction on the defendant's business is a relevant element; where irreparable mischief would ensue to the defendant, it ought not to be granted, especially if the plaintiff would not be injured by delay or can be protected by an interim accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity balances the degree of mischief to each party; if the plaintiff can be adequately protected by money account and delay would irreparably harm defendant, the court may refuse or impose conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad discretionary factors and power to impose conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: In acting on applications for temporary injunctions there is much latitude for discretion: the application may be granted or refused unconditionally, or terms may be imposed on either party as conditions for making or refusing the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts consider the state of the litigation, the nature of the improvement, the character and extent of the infringement, and the comparative inconvenience which will be occasioned to the respective parties; conditions (e.g., bond, accounting, limitation) are commonly used to tailor relief.
